The structure of Ca12Cr2Rh4 (reduced formula Ca6CrRh2) crystallizes in the trigonal space group R-3 (No. 143), with 18 atoms per unit cell distributed over three independent Wyckoff orbits. Geometry-derived analysis shows Ca centers with 11 geometric neighbors (4 Ca, 1 Cr, 6 Rh), Cr centers with 11 neighbors (3 Ca, 8 Rh), and Rh centers with 9 neighbors (6 Ca, 3 Rh), with neighbor distances spanning roughly 3.16–3.67 Å. The geometric neighbor graph forms a single three-dimensional component containing all 18 sites. Validated polyhedron-sharing relations include corner- and edge-sharing between 9-vertex Rh polyhedra and between 11-vertex Ca polyhedra.
